atlas_home_region_card.compact: The art-prog road where rock becomes long-form, conceptual, technical, theatrical, and album-centered.
atlas_home_region_card.standard: It expanded rock's scale and vocabulary: long arcs, concept records, odd meters, synthesizers, fantasy imagery, and headphone-ready studio craft became legitimate rock tools.
atlas_home_region_card.deep: The art-prog road where rock becomes long-form, conceptual, technical, theatrical, and album-centered. It expanded rock's scale and vocabulary: long arcs, concept records, odd meters, synthesizers, fantasy imagery, and headphone-ready studio craft became legitimate rock tools.

region_scene_page.compact: Progressive rock grows from late-1960s art ambition into 1970s album culture.
region_scene_page.standard: Progressive rock grows from late-1960s art ambition into 1970s album culture. Pink Floyd's Time, The Moody Blues' Nights in White Satin, Emerson, Lake & Palmer's Lucky Man, and Jethro Tull's Aqualung give the scene its high-recognition landmarks.
region_scene_page.deep: Progressive rock grows from late-1960s art ambition into 1970s album culture. The pleasure is often in development rather than immediate release. Pink Floyd's Time, The Moody Blues' Nights in White Satin, Emerson, Lake & Palmer's Lucky Man, and Jethro Tull's Aqualung give the scene its high-recognition landmarks. From there, the examples move from quick recognition toward medium and deeper scene signals.

mission_detail_history_module.compact: What this route tests: The art-prog road where rock becomes long-form, conceptual, technical, theatrical, and album-centered.
mission_detail_history_module.standard: Progressive rock grows from late-1960s art ambition into 1970s album culture. Pink Floyd, Yes, Genesis, King Crimson, Emerson Lake & Palmer, Rush, and related artists treat the LP as a constructed world and the band as a technical ensemble. It helps place this road in a broader music-history context.
mission_detail_history_module.deep: Progressive rock grows from late-1960s art ambition into 1970s album culture. Pink Floyd, Yes, Genesis, King Crimson, Emerson Lake & Palmer, Rush, and related artists treat the LP as a constructed world and the band as a technical ensemble. It expanded rock's scale and vocabulary: long arcs, concept records, odd meters, synthesizers, fantasy imagery, and headphone-ready studio craft became legitimate rock tools.
